title: Tor amplitude of a bounded projective complex after scalar restriction
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\rho:A\to B$ a ring homomorphism, and $C^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $B$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $r,s\in\mathbf Z$ and $d\in\mathbf N$. Assume $C^t=0$ whenever $t<r$ or $s<t$, every $C^t$ is projective (maps out of it lift through surjective module maps), and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B,M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and $j>d$, with B restricted along rho [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. In a chosen derived category of A-modules [def-pc-derived-category], scalar restriction of $C^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude $[r-d,s]$: its derived tensor with every A-module in degree zero has vanishing homology in each degree $i<r-d$ or $s<i$. No order hypothesis on r and s and no finite generation are imposed.

source.place: Tags 066H (lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex), 066K (lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings), and 0655; bounded-projective special case of 066K used in Tag 0B6G condition (3). Source checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H.

proof.text: For an A-module M choose a free resolution F concentrated in nonpositive cochain degrees. It is bounded above and flat, hence K-flat, so Tot(C restricted to A tensor_A F) computes the derived tensor. The tensor balancing isomorphism identifies this double complex with C tensor_B (B tensor_A F). Its column in C-degree p has homology C^p tensor_B Tor^A_{-q}(B,M): tensor_B with a projective B-module is exact. This is zero for q>0 or q<-d by the resolution and assumed Tor bound.

source.place: Tags 066H (lemma-tor-amplitude-finite-complex), 066K (lemma-tor-amplitude-change-rings), and 0655; bounded-projective special case of 066K used in Tag 0B6G condition (3). Source checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066K and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066H.

proof.text: Filter the total complex by C-degree. Since C has only finitely many nonzero degrees, this is a finite filtration and its spectral sequence converges with E1^{p,q} the column homology just computed. For n<r-d or s<n and p+q=n, either p lies outside [r,s] and the whole column is zero, or q lies outside [-d,0] and E1 is zero. Later pages are subquotients, so every associated graded piece of H^n is zero. A finite filtration with zero graded pieces is zero. This proves the required bound for each M.

proof.text: If r>s, for each integer t either t<r or s<t; hence all C terms vanish. The double complex is zero, so the same conclusion holds in every degree. This also covers zero rings, zero modules, and empty support intervals.

lean.statement:
theorem boundedProjective_restriction_torAmplitude
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ρ : A →+* B)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
    (r s : ℤ) (hdegrees : ∀ t : ℤ, t < r ∨ s < t → IsZero (C.X t))
    (hprojective : ∀ t : ℤ, Projective (C.X t)) (d : ℕ)
    (hTor : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} A, ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ρ).obj (ModuleCat.of B B))).obj M)) :
    DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} A) (r - (d : ℤ)) s
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ρ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C))
